analysis.headline: Stocks were mixed Wednesday (Dow down 561 points, or 1.1%, S&P 500 down about 0.2% for a fifth straight loss, Nasdaq up 0.4%), and futures are sharply higher this morning, led by Nasdaq 100 futures up about 2%, ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut.
analysis.summary: Wednesday's Dow drop was mostly health insurers: UnitedHealth fell about 10% and Humana about 13% as investors weighed a federal proposal to expand Medicare Advantage audits, while Nvidia gave back an early post-earnings gain and closed down about 2.9% despite revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. Rate worries added pressure: minutes of the Fed's October meeting, released Wednesday afternoon, said almost all officials see further rate hikes as likely appropriate, with a couple open to more than a quarter point in December, and the 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.07%. That higher-for-longer outlook and a firm dollar pushed gold to about $3,725 an ounce, its weakest in more than a year, and Bitcoin fell about 3% to near $62,500, while WTI crude dropped about 3% to roughly $83 after a surprise build in U.S. crude stocks. This morning the mood has flipped toward AI optimism, with S&P 500 futures up about 1.2% and on track for the index's first gain in six sessions, as Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its earlier $70 to $78 range, and Walmart's revenue of $188.8 billion came in just above estimates.
drivers: Fed minutes: almost all officials expect more rate hikes; Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed's Hammack dissented in October in favor of a hike, and a December 8-9 hike is widely priced in

helium.headline: North American Helium has started production at Canada's largest helium field.
helium.summary: The Stewart Valley plant is producing approximately 73 MMcf/Y. A new purification facility opened in southwest Saskatchewan. The company raised CAD $4.9m in a third public offering. Market supply is tightening.

realestate.headline: The Portland housing market is stagnant with slowing sales.
realestate.summary: Sellers are lowering prices to help buyers make deals. Home sales slow as buyers adjust to elevated mortgage rates. Some homebuyers are backing out of deals. Metro approved funding to reduce rents on nearly 300 affordable apartments.
